correctness.rationale: The scalar complement acts fixed-point-freely, so the nonlinear irreducibles are precisely inductions from the free complement-orbits on nontrivial additive characters. The induced-character kernel is the trace-orthogonal complement of the F_p-span of aH. That span is aF_p(H), and F_p(H)=F_{p^e} for e=ord_m(p), giving kernel size p^(f-e), degree m, and codegree p^e. The linear characters come from the cyclic abelianization C_m and contribute codegree d with multiplicity phi(d). Since p^e>m, the recovery formulas are unambiguous. The packaged checker directly verifies the finite-field linear algebra in six cases.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete pseudo-algebra formula and exact rigidity theorem for a standard infinite family of solvable Frobenius groups, in a setting where the invariant is known not to determine even group order globally. The nonlinear codegree has a clean structural interpretation as the size of the minimal subfield containing the complement, while its multiplicity recovers the ambient field size. This is a natural complete classification fact, not a finite census or a routine restatement of the Frobenius character degrees.
